meta.title: iOS parity — 2026-08-19 addendum
meta.purpose: What the web app gained after the 2026-08 parity round, plus the places that round is now WRONG. Read alongside ios-parity-2026-08.json, not instead of it.
meta.product_direction: Unchanged: iOS is the flagship, parity is the floor.
needs_sql_run_first: 0209_event_hosts.sql — event hosts (WS-N1) cannot work until this is applied
meta.conventions: Same as the standing round: each web lib/*.ts seam maps to a Swift Services/*Service.swift; RPCs use an Encodable param struct + .rpc(). ios_targets are NOT proposed here — follow the standing round's per-area docs.
caveats: Generated from the web repo (migrations + CLAUDE.md + the PR list), not from the iOS checkout — iosStatus is inferred from what CLAUDE.md records about the native app.
Every RPC and column named here was read out of the migration files, but ALWAYS re-grep supabase/migrations/ before wiring a parameter name: Supabase keys RPC args by NAME.

read_first: docs/ios-parity-2026-08-19.md — the prose for this addendum
The three CORRECTIONS at its top — they stop you building bugs the web already fixed
Then the ONE area doc you're building, from the standing round
how_to_use.blockers_still_apply: The 2026-08 round's 5 true blockers (how_to_use.true_blockers in its JSON — signed media reads first) come BEFORE anything here. Nothing in this addendum matters if photos 403.
how_to_use.priority_field_warning: There is deliberately no `priority` field in this addendum — in the standing round agents read 'blocking' as 'foundational' and marked 24 items blocking, including screens iOS already had. Use suggested_order.

status_values.has-it-audit-depth: iOS has a version and the web one grew
status_values.wrong-in-spec: the standing spec describes this incorrectly — read the correction before building

no_ios_work.reason: Server-side or documentation only — read and move on.

items.what: Search indexer stopped polling; reconciles on realtime change and on search. Mini-side only.
Never email the App Store reviewer account. Server-side.

no_ios_work.mini_restart_required: The event-email and house-request emails need a mini git pull + restart (Admin → Media server) before anything goes out.

workstreams.title: Family Fest: Past Years + starting a new year

features.name: Family Fest season has FIVE phases
features.whatItDoes: A finished fest must say so instead of rendering a countdown to its own past start date, which clamps to zero and reads 'Family Fest is on'.
gotchas: off-season and concluded are BOTH quiet but are NOT the same phase — off-season means the window is still AHEAD, concluded means it is behind us. Collapsing them is the original bug.
isTakeover must be spelled out as isPlanning||isLive||isWrap, NOT phase !== 'off-season' — the negation counts a finished fest as a takeover.
Empty/malformed dates must be guarded to off-season explicitly: every comparison against NaN is false, so they otherwise fall through and report a fest with no dates as concluded.
Supersedes part of docs/ios-parity-2026-08/13-family-fest.md.

features.name: fest_config is read as MANY rows
features.whatItDoes: The current fest is the NEWEST fest_config row, not a compiled-in year — which is what makes an archive and an in-app new year possible.
gotchas: iOS currently mirrors the web's old hardcoded FEST_YEAR = 2026.
No new table, column or migration — purely how the rows are read.
The fest week is decided by a family POLL every year. Never default or compute it from the previous year.

features.name: can_manage_event is no longer 'admin OR creator'
features.whatItDoes: Any screen deciding whether to show Edit/Delete/add-attendee on an event must not hardcode the old predicate.
gotchas: Supersedes the permission model in docs/ios-parity-2026-08/09-events-and-cabins.md.

⚠️⚠️ THE HOST PANEL MUST OWN ITS OWN LIST. On web this shipped rendering a `hosts` prop threaded from the parent, and only ONE of the three surfaces that mount the event sheet passed a refresh. Picking a committee wrote the row, the picker closed, and the panel still said 'Nobody yet' — the click looked like it did nothing while the database had the host. Load hosts inside the host panel on appear and refetch after every add/remove; treat anything handed in as a first-paint seed only.

⚠️ This is the SECOND time this shape hit the same screen (web PR #572 was 'Add someone to an event does nothing', same cause). A fix that says 'the parent must refetch' does not survive the next caller. Own the fetch where the mutation happens.
⚠️ A write that returns no error but changes nothing must SAY SO. A silent success and a silent failure look identical, which is what made the web bug need a database query to diagnose.

⚠️ NO HOST IS A COMPLETE ANSWER, not an unfinished form — a holiday weekend has nobody running it, somebody may put an event on the calendar without hosting it, and blank is the DEFAULT for every event. Don't word the empty state as a gap to fill ('Nobody yet — name a host'); word it as how the event currently works, with naming one offered as the optional narrowing it is. Also say what removing the last host DOES: it hands the event back to the whole family.
Synthesized events (holiday weekends, Family Fest) have no `events` row and therefore no creator, so they are permanently hostless and should not offer a host editor at all.

features.name: The house requests board
features.whatItDoes: Every 'should we?' ask for a house, grouped by status, with a permanent legend explaining the three kinds.
gotchas: App admins have NO authority here (0202): only that house's House Admins may decide, and only the author + that house's members may see the board.
The read policy compares house_id DIRECTLY rather than calling is_house_member(), which grants app admins a blanket pass and would silently re-open cross-house reads.
Use a COLUMN-GROUP LADDER on the select: an unknown column fails the whole select with 42703 and renders an empty board, which then reads as 'migration missing'.
numeric comes back from PostgREST as a STRING — coerce it or every cost sum is string concatenation.
Never name only the paperwork: migration 0205 exists because 'Purchase Request' told House Admins nothing about whose money or who orders. Show the per-kind 'deal' line everywhere a kind appears.
There is NO default kind — picking one is its own step and the form does not exist until chosen.

features.whatItDoes: Keeps the title, reason, links, photos, discussion and approval; asks only for the total and receipt.

REQUESTER-ONLY, and that's correctness not preference: a reimbursement pays created_by, so anyone else converting would route the money to whoever ASKED rather than whoever PAID.
The approval survives; re-approval is demanded only when the amount exceeds the approved estimate by more than the grace ($25).
quantity is CLEARED on conversion — on a receipt the total already covers however many.

features.name: House Admins
features.whatItDoes: A leadership tier for a house, so it can run its own money decisions without an app admin.
gotchas: Only an app admin who is THEMSELVES in that house may appoint one — not any app admin, and not a House Admin promoting peers.
profiles.house_admin is in no client update grant; the RPC is the only write path.
Changing houses CLEARS the flag, or someone reassigned keeps approver rights over their new house.
is_house_admin is strict — no app-admin override. Use can_review_house_request for permission checks.

features.name: Four notification kinds
features.whatItDoes: Submitted (to House Admins), decision (to the requester), handled (to the OTHER approvers), and the order-in-time reminder.
gotchas: A house-scoped request notifies that house's House Admins and NOBODY else — no app-admin fallback (0199 fixed one vacuum request paging all 7 app admins).
All four kinds need adding to the iOS pushable set.
EVERY send must name its recipients in the UI first — the composer shows the resolved list, read from the SAME predicate the server fan-out uses.

features.name: 'Just test it — only notify me'
features.whatItDoes: Runs a real request through the whole pipeline while notifying only its author and staying hidden from the house.
gotchas: The client must REFUSE to fall back pre-0200 when the flag is set — silently dropping a 'notify just me' would page the whole house.

features.name: Delete, and the 7-day tombstone
features.whatItDoes: Removing a request leaves a tombstone for 7 days instead of vanishing.
gotchas: A still-PENDING request is deliberately NOT deletable (unless it's a test): a denial leaves a note and a name, a deletion just makes the ask evaporate.
Approved-but-unordered is also not deletable — that's the state the feature exists to keep visible.
Mirror the SQL gate client-side so the button only appears where the RPC would succeed.

features.name: Order-in-time nudge
features.whatItDoes: A card on the board when there are approved-but-unordered purchases and somebody will be at the house soon.
gotchas: Purchases only — a reimbursement needs paying, an idea has nothing to buy.
Runs on pg_cron, not the mini. The mini only relays the push.
It offers the other explanation too ('already bought it? mark it ordered') — nagging an admin about a job they already did is how a reminder gets muted.
Known limit: Family Fest is synthesized in client code, not an events row, so SQL can't see it and it won't trigger a reminder.

features.name: Preview the event email before sending
features.whatItDoes: Shows the REAL rendered email with a pager across every version that will go out, each labelled with how many people it reaches.
gotchas: ONE SEND PER AUDIENCE, not one email: a house-scoped work item is visible only to that house, so recipients come back pre-sorted into buckets (one per house with items, plus 'general'). A person lands in exactly one.
The house copy SAYS it's the house copy; the general copy stays completely silent that a hidden list exists.
event_attendance now has THREE FKs to profiles (user_id, sponsor_user_id, added_by) — any embed MUST name the FK explicitly or PostgREST returns PGRST201 instead of data.
No link to the app anywhere, by decision: a bare link opens the browser, which on iOS is a separate signed-out session.
The sender is NAMED and CC'd on every send, with replyTo pointing at them.
Completed work items are excluded outright from the email.

The preview is a DRY RUN of the same SQL the real send uses, returning per-bucket counts and NO addresses. Never assemble it client-side: a house-scoped item is RLS-invisible to a non-member, so the client would render a different email than the one that sends.

features.whatItDoes: Delivers the event's details plus exactly what's assigned to it.
gotchas: ONE SEND PER AUDIENCE, not one email: a house-scoped work item is visible only to that house, so recipients come back pre-sorted into buckets (one per house with items, plus 'general'). A person lands in exactly one.

set_house_request_progress-style claim columns: sent_buckets records each bucket as it succeeds so a retry doesn't re-send.
Needs a mini git pull + restart before anything actually goes out.

features.name: Manually add someone to an event's RSVP list
features.whatItDoes: Three separate entry points on purpose: an app member, a family_roster person with no account, or a typed outside guest.
gotchas: ONE SEND PER AUDIENCE, not one email: a house-scoped work item is visible only to that house, so recipients come back pre-sorted into buckets (one per house with items, plus 'general'). A person lands in exactly one.
The house copy SAYS it's the house copy; the general copy stays completely silent that a hidden list exists.

No link to the app anywhere, by decision: a bare link opens the browser, which on iOS is a separate signed-out session.
The sender is NAMED and CC'd on every send, with replyTo pointing at them.
Completed work items are excluded outright from the email.
A guest's SPONSOR is required — picked from a dropdown, never typed — so an outside guest is always traceable.
A guest's email is optional and scoped to THIS one event only.
Collapsing the two entry points into one 'type a name' box is the confusion this feature exists to fix.

⚠️ It is TWO RPCs, not one: add_event_family_member (a member OR a family_roster person) and add_event_guest (a typed outside guest, sponsor required). They are deliberately separate entry points — collapsing them into one 'type a name' box is the confusion 0196 exists to fix.

features.name: The concluded fest state
features.whatItDoes: The hub says thank you and links the archive; the RSVP card and the finished week step aside; the sub-nav drops to Overview + Past Years.
gotchas: Read correction C1 first.

features.name: Past Years — the archive of finished fests
features.whatItDoes: A list of finished fests, each opening its whole week read-only: schedule, dinners, menus, leads.
gotchas: NO edit affordances for ANYONE including admins — the editor writes to the CURRENT year, so its sheets would edit the wrong fest.
NO sign-up cards — there's nothing left to sign up for.
KEEP tournament brackets, read-only: who won the musky tournament is the history worth archiving.
No seed fallback: backfilling an empty year with the in-code seed would FABRICATE history.
A year appears here purely from its dates, on the same WRAP_TAIL_DAYS threshold as the concluded phase.

features.name: Start planning next year
features.whatItDoes: Creates a new fest year and optionally copies last year's plan across as a starting point.
gotchas: INSERT a new row; NEVER edit the current one's dates — that drags the finished fest forward so its archive describes a week that never happened.
Dates are typed in BY HAND and start EMPTY: the week is decided by a family poll and cannot be derived from last year.
The template copy deliberately omits sign-up config and tournament flags — per-year live state keyed to specific dates.

features.name: A fifth work-item urgency: custom
features.whatItDoes: Free-text timing wording plus a picked colour, for something more specific than the fixed tiers.
gotchas: ALWAYS resolve through urgencyMeta(item), never by indexing the fixed table — a custom item has no entry there.
urgencyRank takes the whole item so custom can rank between This year and Next year.

features.name: Recurring work items
features.whatItDoes: A task due every N years reappears as a fresh open item instead of vanishing when checked off.
gotchas: The next cycle is stamped surface_on = Jan 1 of the year it's next due, not the exact anniversary.
Rows with a FUTURE surface_on must be filtered OUT of the list — they exist immediately so the recurrence is never lost.
Deliberately NO notification on the auto-created copy (suppressed via a session GUC).

features.name: Any member can create an event
features.whatItDoes: Was admin-only end to end.
gotchas: Editing/deleting is admin OR the event's creator — and since 0209, hosts. See WS-N1.
A non-admin creator must NOT see the Reminders section; scheduled reminders ride the admin-only broadcast queue.

features.name: Pick an event's work items from the existing checklist
features.whatItDoes: Multi-select over existing open items, each showing its urgency and scope, with a create-new escape hatch.
gotchas: Unlinking never deletes the item itself.

⚠️ add_work_item_to_event is declared in 0050 WITHOUT a schema prefix (`create or replace function add_work_item_to_event`), unlike almost every other RPC in this codebase. It resolves to public via search_path, but a grep for 'function public.add_work_item_to_event' finds nothing — don't conclude it doesn't exist.

features.name: Group an event's work items by scope
features.whatItDoes: Around the Resort first, then one group per house — with a locked count line for a house you're not in.
gotchas: A house-scoped item is RLS-invisible to a non-member, so a plain read silently drops it — the count RPC is the only way to show it exists at all.
That RPC is SECURITY DEFINER and therefore gated on is_approved_member(). ANY new SECURITY DEFINER read needs the same check.
Removing an item must refetch the house COUNTS too, not just the items.

features.name: 'In the house' is three kinds of person
features.whatItDoes: A housemate with an account, someone assigned to the house who isn't on the app yet, and a guest sponsored by a housemate.
gotchas: The web derivation used to open `if (!row.userId) continue`, silently dropping the roster and guest cases.
'A real stay always wins' must be guarded on userId — house_stays.created_by is a uuid, so no real stay can belong to a roster person or guest, and matching a null suppresses all of them at once.
Key a derived row on the ATTENDANCE ROW's id, not the user id, or two guests at one event collapse into one person.
fetchHouseRosterMembers returns only UNLINKED roster slots — a claimed one is already covered by profiles.house_id and would list the person twice.

features.name: One derivation for 'who's here on day X'
features.whatItDoes: The calendar's day detail and the who's-staying list must agree.
gotchas: The web's day popover read house_stays only and said 'Staying (0)' while the list below it showed five people for the same dates. Do not derive it twice.
The heading count is PEOPLE, not rows: a stay's guest_names count and nobody is double-counted.
